ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.44 (voucher per NS-7) to the rider for the non-exempt detour segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (no account flag — RD-6 threshold not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was RydeTAXI (metered), so the fare model is per-km and detour kilometres feed the meter [F4][F6][RD-1][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists: 21:47–21:50, 1.76 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.03 km, +1.73 km, up to 979 m off route [F3]. No traffic incident excuses it — F13 records no incidents near the route, and the speed-band facts (SELETAR band 4, TAMPINES band 5) are not band 1/2 and are expressly corroborative only, so RD-4(a) and (b) do not exempt this segment [F11][F12][F13][RD-4].

RD-3(a) also fails: this trace records no measured stop inside the segment, and the rider never named a place — the driver's own words propose "the petrol station just ahead" [F7][F3][RD-3]. The rider's "Sure, no problem" is agreement to a stop at a place the driver chose and never named, so the rider-requested-stop exemption does not reach the extra kilometres (RD-3(b) rationale: the rider consented to "pull in", not to that route change) [F7][F8][RD-3].

RD-5 is where the scope question bites. The rider did agree, before the segment started (21:44 reply to the 21:43 message, segment begins 21:47), and a one-minute pull-in at the station "just ahead" ties itself by timing to the very next off-route movement, so the distance to that station is exempt [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. But the exemption is confined to the route the driver actually named — a brief stop at a station just ahead. The rider never agreed to a 1.73 km loop, and the record shows no petrol stop took place at all, so the segment far exceeds the named scope: it is not "that route" the driver proposed but an unnamed excursion, and the excess is not covered by the rider's consent [F3][F7][F8][F10][RD-5]. The driver's statement that the rider "agreed to a short stop" is a post-hoc claim, not consent, and in any case it concedes only a short stop (G11) [F10][RD-5]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so nothing here is undetermined: the meaning and timing of both messages are clear, and the finding is "counts" for the excess [F9][RD-5].

The exempt core of the segment is the station pull-in itself, measured by the 979 m maximum deviation recorded for this segment; the remainder is non-exempt: 1.73 km − 0.979 km = 0.751 km [F3]. Applying the trace formula (distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km = $1.4102/km): 0.751 km × $1.4102/km = $1.0600 → $1.06 [F4][F6][RD-2]. The whole-table excess billed of $2.90 (2.1 km) covers more than this single measured segment and includes map-matching residual, which RD-2 does not refund [F1][F4][RD-2]. The result is therefore refund_partial of $1.06 on a $40.18 RydeTAXI fare [F6][RD-2].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this breach is not "repeated" and no account flag follows [F16][RD-6]. The rider's baseline is clean and irrelevant to this disposition [F15]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement; the complaint alleges a fare/scope grievance, and F7, F8 and F10 contain ordinary coordination language with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 is required [F7][F8][F10].

events.body:
RIDER: Your fare dispute is settled: you are getting a $2.44 refund, paid as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: your driver took a 1.73 km detour off the best route, and that stretch was not covered by anything that would make it chargeable — there was no traffic problem on the route, and your "sure, no problem" reply agreed only to a brief pull-in at a spot just ahead, not to a 1.73 km loop. No petrol stop actually happened.

Nothing changes on your account. Thanks for flagging it.

DRIVER: This fare dispute is settled: $2.44 of the trip is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: the 1.73 km stretch off the best route between 21:47 and 21:50 was not exempt. There was no traffic problem on that route, and the rider's earlier reply agreed only to a brief pull-in just ahead — not to that diversion — and no stop took place.

A route breach is recorded on your file. Your account is not flagged, since this is your first upheld route dispute in 90 days.
